date_note: Date is Marui Group's announcement of 20 November; PLAID notified Marui of the unauthorized access on 13 November.
title: Marui Group: about 8.83 million and about 8.5 million customer records leaked via PLAID KARTE breach
summary: Marui Group said on 20 November that customer data leaked after unauthorized access to PLAID's KARTE, which it says came from PLAID's system, not Marui's. About 8.83 million people (name, gender, date of birth, email, customer management number) and about 8.5 million EPOS CARD users incl. former members (customer management number, gender) are affected; about 60,000 of them may also have name, age, annual income and cash-advance limit exposed. Card numbers are not confirmed leaked.
plain: Marui Group says data of about 8.83 million web customers and about 8.5 million EPOS CARD users leaked via PLAID's KARTE. Card numbers are not confirmed leaked.
exec: About 8.83 million and about 8.5 million customer records at a retailer and card issuer exposed through a vendor's marketing tool.
action: Marui and EPOS CARD customers: be careful with suspicious emails and do not open URLs in them or enter personal information, as Marui Group advises.

validation.note: Marui Group's own notice (primary) read, agreeing with Cybersecurity.com's report on the figures.

review.note: Compared title, figures (8.83M, 8.5M, 60,000), data types, card statement and date against Marui notice and Cybersecurity.com; all match. Fixed action: notice gives general suspicious-email/URL advice, not a warning about Marui/EPOS impersonation by phone.
